source_text: Si de exomologesi retractas, gehennam in corde considera, quam tibi exomologesis exstinguit: et poenae prius magnitudinem imaginare, ut de remedii adeptione non dubites. Quid illum thesaurum ignis aeterni aestimamus, cum fumariola quaedam ejus tales flammarum ictus suscitent, ut proximae urbes aut jam nullae exstent, aut idem sibi de die sperent. Dissiliunt superbissimi montes ignis intrinsecus foetu: et quod nobis judicii perpetuitatem probat, cum dissiliant, cum devorentur, nunquam tamen finiuntur. Quis haec supplicia interim montium non judicii minantis exemplaria deputabit? Quis scintillas tales non magni alicujus et inaestimabilis foci missilia quaedam et exercitoria jacula consentiet? Igitur cum scias adversus gehennam post prima illa intinctionis dominicae munimenta, esse adhuc in exomologesi secunda subsidia, cur salutem tuam deseris? Cur cessas aggredi, quod scias mederi tibi? Mutae quidem animae et irrationales, medicinas sibi divinitus attributas in tempore agnoscunt. Cervus sagitta transfixus, ut ferrum et irrevocabiles moras ejus de vulnere expellat scit sibi dictamno medendum. Hirundo, si excaecaverit pullos, novit illos oculare rursus de sua chelidonia. Peccator restituendo sibi institutam a Domino exomologesin sciens, praeteribit illam? quae Babylonium regem in regna restituit? Diu enim poenitentiam Domino immolarat, septenni squalore exomologesin operatus, unguium leoninum in modum efferatione, et capilli incuria horrorem aquilinum praeferente. Proh malae tractationis? quem homines perhorrebant, Deus recipiebat. Contra autem aegyptius imperator, qui populum Dei aliquando afflictum, diu Domino suo denegatum persecutus, in praelium irruit, post tot documenta plagarum, dissidio maris, quod soli populo pervium licebat, revolutis fluctibus perit. Poenitentiam enim et ministerium ejus exomologesin abjecerat. Quid ergo ultra de istis duabus humanae salutis quasi plancis, styli potius negotium quam officium conscientiae meae curans? peccator enim omnium notarum cum sim, nec ulli rei nisi poenitentiae natus, non facile possum super illa tacere, quam ipse quoque et stirpis humanae et offensae in Dominum princeps Adam exomologesi restitutus in paradisum suum, non tacet.
pass_a_gloss: If you retract from confession, consider Gehenna in your heart, which confession extinguishes for you: and first imagine the magnitude of the punishment, so that you may not doubt the acquisition of the remedy. What do we esteem that treasure of eternal fire, when certain sparks of it stir up such blows of flames, that neighboring cities either no longer exist, or hope the same for themselves from day to day. The most proud mountains burst apart with fire inwardly conceived: and what proves to us the perpetuity of judgment, when they burst apart, when they are devoured, they are never nevertheless finished. Who will not consider these punishments of the mountains meanwhile as examples of threatening judgment? Who will not agree that such sparks are certain missiles and exercising darts of a great and inestimable fire? Therefore, when you know that against Gehenna, after the first defenses of the Lord's baptism, there are still second subsidies in confession, why do you desert your salvation? Why do you cease to attack what you know heals you? Indeed, mute and irrational souls recognize in time the medicines divinely attributed to them. A deer pierced by an arrow, so that it may expel the iron and its irretrievable delays from the wound, knows that it must be healed by dittany. A swallow, if it has blinded its young, knows that it must restore their sight again with its chelidony. A sinner, knowing that confession instituted by the Lord is to restore himself, will pass by it? which restored the king of Babylon to his kingdom? For he had long immolated repentance to the Lord, having worked confession in a seven-year squalor, with a lion-like fierceness of his nails, and a horror of his hair, neglecting it, preferring an eagle-like appearance. Oh, the bad treatment! whom men shuddered at, God received. But, on the other hand, the Egyptian emperor, who had at some time afflicted the people of God, and long denied his Lord, rushing into battle, after so many documents of plagues, the discord of the sea, which was only allowed to be passed through by his people, having been rolled back in waves, perished. For he had rejected repentance and the ministry of its confession. What, therefore, do I still care about these two things, like two planks of human salvation, rather taking care of the business of my style than the office of my conscience? For I, being a sinner of all notes, and born for nothing except repentance, cannot easily be silent about it, which also the prince Adam, the first of the human race and of the offense against the Lord, restored by confession, does not keep silent about, having been restored to his paradise.

pass_b_english: If you pull back from confession, fix Gehenna in your heart — confession is what puts it out for you. First, picture the sheer scale of the punishment, so you stop doubting the remedy exists. What do we make of that treasure of eternal fire, when mere sparks of it kick up flame-storms that leave neighboring cities either erased or waiting each day for the same fate? The proudest mountains burst apart from fire conceived inside them; and here is proof of judgment's eternity: they burst, they burn, yet they never finish. Who would not read these mountain torments as samples of the judgment that threatens? Who would not agree such sparks are missiles and practice-darts from a great and inestimable furnace? So, since you know that after the first defenses of the Lord's baptism, second reinforcements still stand in confession against Gehenna, why abandon your salvation? Why stop attacking what you know heals you? Even mute, irrational creatures recognize in time the medicines God assigned them. A deer pierced by an arrow knows to expel the iron and its deathly grip from the wound with dittany. A swallow that has blinded its chicks knows to restore their sight with celandine. Will a sinner, knowing the confession instituted by the Lord restores him, walk past it — the same confession that restored the king of Babylon to his kingdom? For a long time he offered repentance to the Lord, working confession through seven years of squalor, his nails grown fierce like a lion's, his neglected hair presenting an eagle-like horror. Oh, the wretched treatment! — the man men shuddered at, God received. But the Egyptian emperor, who once afflicted God's people and long denied his Lord, charged into battle; after so many documented plagues, the sea's parting — passable only for that people — rolled back its waves and he perished. For he had rejected repentance and the ministry of its confession. What more, then, should I say about these two planks of human salvation, when I am looking after the business of my style rather than the office of my conscience? For I, a sinner of every stripe, born for nothing but repentance, cannot easily keep silent about it — the very thing the prince Adam, first of the human race and first to offend the Lord, restored by confession to his paradise, does not keep silent about either.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Latin text, including the complex descriptions of the king of Babylon's appearance and the comparison between the Egyptian emperor and the people of God. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source. The distinction between 'styli negotium' and 'conscientiae officium' is preserved.
